item.title: Drupal Security Team Warns Second RCE Flaw Is Actively Exploited
item.description:
Drupal Security Team Warns Second RCE Flaw Is Actively Exploited

The Drupal security team announced that attackers are exploiting a second critical vulnerability that allows them to breach and hijack unpatched websites. This follows the recent patching of a remote code execution flaw known as CVE-2026-132165, or Fail2Install, which allowed anonymous users to take over vulnerable sites by abusing the Drupal installer. An update to the original security advisory warned that threat actors began exploiting the initial flaw one day after patches were released.

🧩 The New Vulnerability

The new security issue, tracked as CVE-2026-136716, was patched one week after the initial release. It addresses attack vectors that were left unpatched in the previous advisory and also enables attackers to hijack vulnerable Drupal sites. While most installations are covered by the patch, certain sites in unusual or incomplete install states remain vulnerable to site takeover, including production environments.

🔍 Detection Challenges

According to Drupal, it is not apparent in the user interface if a site is in the affected vulnerable state. Furthermore, sites that are already compromised may no longer be in the vulnerable state. The team emphasized that this issue is being exploited in the wild, and any site that left its installer remotely accessible following SA-CORE-2026-017 may still have been compromised.

⚙️ Recommended Actions

Drupal has warned users that any unsecured website may have been compromised and advised administrators to ensure the user 1 email address is one they control, considering a reset if necessary. Site logs should be checked for unauthorized access, with a focus on unexpected changes to or by the user 1 account.

For those who cannot immediately upgrade to Drupal 10.6.23, 11.3.23, or 11.4.14, the following mitigation is recommended:

  • Secure the installer on all new and existing sites by blocking access to /core/install.php in the web server configuration or the .htaccess file in the web root.
  • Follow the provided guide if evidence suggests the site may have been compromised.

💡 Broader Context

The US Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) has flagged six Drupal security flaws as being abused in the wild since November 2021. Two of these flaws have also been exploited in ransomware attacks.

#Drupal #Security #CVE-2026-136716 #WebSecurity #VulnerabilityManagement

Source: Drupal warns of new site takeover flaw exploited in attacks

item.title: NGINX HTTP/2 Use‑After‑Free (CVE‑2026‑123633) Enables DoS and Potential Code Execution
item.description:
NGINX HTTP/2 Use‑After‑Free (CVE‑2026‑123633) Enables DoS and Potential Code Execution

🔍 Overview

  • CVE-2026-123633 is a use-after-free vulnerability in NGINX HTTP/2.
  • Allows an unauthenticated attacker to cause denial of service; code execution may be possible when address space layout randomization (ASLR) is disabled or bypassed.

🧩 How it works

  • A fragmented HTTP/2 request can leave an active connection marked as reusable.
  • Under connection pressure, NGINX may close that connection and free memory still used by the active request.
  • When a hostname is resolved during the request and free worker connections run low, the DNS resolver may read from freed memory.
  • The function ngx_http_v2_create_stream() leaves the reusable mark set; the fix clears it with ngx_reusable_connection(…).

⚙️ Key details

  • Affected NGINX versions: 1.19.7‑1.30.6 and 1.31.0‑1.31.8 (medium severity on NGINX advisory).
  • Fixed in NGINX 1.30.7 (stable) and 1.31.9 (mainline).
  • F5 CVE record scores 9.2 Critical (CVSS 4.0) and 8.1 High (CVSS 3.1).
  • Reported by memN0ps (Palo Alto Networks Unit 42).
  • CVE-2026-123634 is a separate DNS resolver vulnerability fixed in the same release.
  • Independent reproduction with AddressSanitizer on unmodified NGINX 1.31.7 and 1.31.8 stopped at the first read from freed DNS lookup memory.
  • Pre‑authentication remote code execution was achieved on a non‑root NGINX worker under a non‑default configuration; some attempts did not open a shell.

🚀 Availability

  • Fixes are included in NGINX 1.30.7 (stable) and 1.31.9 (mainline).
  • F5 also lists affected NGINX Plus releases.

💡 Why it matters

  • Use‑after‑free can lead to denial of service and, under certain conditions, remote code execution.
  • The vulnerability demonstrates a serious risk in HTTP/2 connection handling that affects a wide range of NGINX deployments.

#NGINX #CVE2026 #HTTP2 #Security #UseAfterFree

Source: NGINX HTTP/2 Use-After-Free: CVE-2026-123633

item.title: GitHub Login Plugin for agent.datasette.io Receives 1.0 Release
item.description:
GitHub Login Plugin for agent.datasette.io Receives 1.0 Release

The GitHub login plugin used on the agent.datasette.io demo site has received a 1.0 release. The update resolves an issue where authenticated user sessions were expiring prematurely due to missing cookie parameters.

🔍 Overview

While running the GitHub login plugin on the agent.datasette.io demo site, it was observed that authenticated sessions were not lasting very long. Investigation revealed that the plugin was setting cookies without a Max-Age parameter. Consequently, these cookies were expiring at the end of a browser session. This behavior occurs frequently in Mobile Safari, regardless of how the application is being used.

⚙️ Key details

The update includes the following changes and technical details:

  • Session Fix: The cookie expiration issue was resolved in pull request #80 by addressing the missing Max-Age parameter.
  • Compatibility: The plugin has been thoroughly tested against both Datasette 0.65.x and Datasette 1.0ax.
  • Version Bump: Because the plugin has been around for a significant period and is fully tested, it has been officially promoted to a 1.0 release.

#Datasette #GitHubLogin #WebDevelopment #SoftwareRelease

Source: Release: datasette-auth-github 1.0
